# Audio Adjuster

> A free, open-source macOS menu bar app that gives every running application its own
> volume slider. Built on Core Audio process taps; macOS 14.2 or later; Apache 2.0.

macOS has one system volume, so turning a video down takes your music with it. Audio
Adjuster adds a per-application volume control: a bar in the menu bar for anything
currently making noise. It is menu bar only — no Dock icon and no window.

## How it works

macOS has no per-app volume API. Since 14.2 it has Core Audio *process taps*, shipped for
screen recording and system-audio capture. A tap can also mute the process it captures,
and that is the half that makes a volume control possible.

For each app you actually adjust, the app creates one private process tap, wraps it in a
private aggregate device built on the current default output, and runs an IO proc that
copies tapped frames to the output with gain applied. Apps you never touch keep their
ordinary path, with no tap and no added latency. There is no kernel extension and no
virtual audio driver.

## Key facts

- Requires macOS 14.2 or later (process taps do not exist before it).
- Free, open source, Apache 2.0. No account, telemetry or paid tier.
- Volume range is 0 to 1000%, with 100% at the slider midpoint: linear below so cuts are
  proportional and reach exact silence, logarithmic above so equal drags are equal
  multiplications.
- Levels are keyed to the bundle identifier, so they survive relaunches and restarts.
- Linked mode holds a constant sum across bars: what one app gains, the others give up.
  It can be switched off so each bar moves alone. Mute is never linked.
- It requests audio-recording permission because macOS gates process taps behind it. It
  reads each app's audio to play it back at your chosen level and records nothing.
- Builds are ad-hoc signed, not notarized, as the project has no Apple Developer ID.
